svg.title: The Aug-28 open-weights decision splits in two: Z.ai holds the big GLM-5.3's weights past their own target while shipping GLM-5.3-Flash with open MIT weights the same week, and the closed ceiling stays frozen a ninth straight brief
svg.desc: A two-branch diagram from a central Aug 28 decision node. The left branch, drawn dashed in amber, is the big GLM-5.3 (744-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts): its open weights were due about August 28 but the target arrived with nothing published — the zai-org GLM-5.3 repository is still only an "upcoming release" placeholder, so the drop slipped. It is held for a stated safety review after an emergent offensive-cyber capability; its general Index of 60 was measured third-party but the download is gated, and its cyber figures remain unreplicated. The right branch, drawn solid in teal, is GLM-5.3-Flash, the viral stealth model that topped OpenRouter for six days as "Ox Alpha": a 320-billion-total, 18-billion-active multimodal mixture-of-experts, shipped with MIT-licensed weights day one, Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 57 (level with Claude Opus 4.8, above DeepSeek V4 Pro at 53), priced $0.15 and $0.50 per million tokens (about one-hundredth of frontier price), served entirely on roughly one hundred thousand domestically-produced Chinese chips, and the biggest launch in OpenRouter history at more than 11 trillion tokens in three days. A footer strip shows the frozen closed ceiling — Claude Opus 5 at 63 and number one, Fable 5 at 62.1, then GPT-5.6 Sol at 61 tying Grok 4.6 at 60.9 — with the two open leaders (the held GLM-5.3 at 60 and Kimi K3 at 60) just below and GLM-5.3-Flash at 57 in the near-frontier band, no Index-64 model and no flagship price cut since July 24, now 35 days, across a ninth straight brief.
svg.text: The open-weights decision splits — one GLM held for danger, another shipped wide open
Aug 28 target arrives. Same lab, same week, opposite calls: the 744B GLM-5.3 slips its own date; GLM-5.3-Flash ships MIT weights day one.
≈ Aug 28 — the decision date
the two-week safety clock ends
◀ GLM-5.3 · 744B MoE (~40B active)
HELD — weights slip their own target
Aug 28 arrives; weights still NOT on Hugging Face.
zai-org/GLM-5.3 = still an "upcoming release" placeholder.
• Held for safety: emergent exploit-chaining
• General Index 60 — measured, but download gated
• Cyber figures (CyberGym 84.5) still unreplicated
Outcome (c): the slip — as Qwen3.8-Max slipped twice
the top open model still ships on a timer, not a link
▶ GLM-5.3-Flash · 320B-A18B MoE
SHIPPED — open MIT weights, day one
Was the stealth "Ox Alpha" — topped OpenRouter 6 days.
First natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series.
• Index 57 — level with Opus 4.8, > DeepSeek V4 Pro 53
• $0.15 / $0.50 per Mtok — ~1/100th of frontier
• Served on ~100k domestic Chinese chips (no Nvidia)
Biggest OpenRouter launch ever: 11T+ tokens / 3 days
Zhipu HK shares +12% on the reveal
Neither reaches the closed ceiling — frozen a 9th straight brief

g.text: top open by score — not downloadable
57 · the open model you can actually download today

svg.text: ❄️ No Index-64 model. No flagship price cut since Jul 24 — 35 days. Gemini 3.5 Pro still absent (3 missed targets). Motion stays entirely below the line.

Index = Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. GLM-5.3-Flash figures vendor/press-reported; the big GLM-5.3 general 60 is third-party, its cyber figures and the domestic-chip vendor mix are not independently confirmed.
